candidates.title: DiLLeMa: An extensible and scalable framework for distributed large language models (LLMs) inference on multi-GPU clusters
candidates.reason: DiLLeMaはRay上に構築しvLLMエンジンを用いてマルチGPUクラスタへLLM推論を分散配置する拡張可能なフレームワークで、負荷並列化と適応的資源管理により推論レイテンシ削減とスケーリングを実現しており、分散推論基盤への直接の貢献である。

candidates.title: DRLM: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based LLM Query Orchestration in Edge Environments
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM) services increasingly process heterogeneous queries with diverse latency, accuracy, and resource requirements. While edge deployment reduces response time, the heterogeneity of devices and the diversity of model families, parameter scales, and quantization levels make efficient LLM query orchestration challenging. This paper introduces DRLM, a Deep Reinforcement Learning-based LLM query orchestration framework in edge environments. DRLM integrates two lightweight predictors: (i) a class-conditioned quality estimator that maps queries to semantic categories and infers model performance, and (ii) a feature-driven latency predictor that estimates inference time across model-device configurations. These predictions, combined with system state, feed a factorized Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent that performs state-aware orchestration decisions. To enable data-driven orchestration, we construct a large-scale benchmarking dataset with 223 835 measurements spanning 1258 queries, 6 query classes, 8 model families (32 deployed instances), 5 quantization levels, and heterogeneous edge devices. Evaluation on a 64-node edge cluster and comparison with three baselines and two state-of-the-art methods show that DRLM reduces inference latency by up to 51% and queuing delay by up to 67 %, while incurring at most 8% accuracy loss. It improves latency under increasing workloads up to 61.4%, demonstrating robust and stable orchestration.
candidates.reason: DRLMはエッジ環境でのLLMクエリ・オーケストレーションを品質推定器とレイテンシ予測器に基づく深層強化学習で行い、モデル・デバイス・量子化レベルの選択により推論レイテンシを最大51%削減する推論スケジューリング手法である。

candidates.title: Cost-Aware LLM Invocation Strategies in Large-Scale Enterprise Systems
candidates.venue: 2026 International Conference Automatics, Robotics and Artificial Intelligence (ICARAI)
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming central to production pipelines at companies of all sizes. At scale, however, a tradeoff emerges: more capable models complete individual tasks more successfully, but charge per-token rates linearly proportional to that capacity. Billions of tokens are served daily at production companies, making this tradeoff one of cost versus quality. Companies that serve millions of requests per day cannot afford cost overruns or spikes in latency. Routing all traffic through a single large model is costly because many requests are simple. In practice, companies use heuristic approaches or manual rulesets that do not transfer well between workflows. In this paper, we address this challenge by presenting CALLS (Cost-Aware LLM Load-balancing Strategy), a strategy for selecting one of a fleet of model tiers for each query based on its estimated complexity. CALLS offers: (i) a lightweight complexity classifier that uses features capturing the syntax and semantics of the input query, (ii) a simple yet expressive three-tier routing policy based on a formalization of the cost-utility tradeoff, and (iii) an online feedback loop that calibrates the complexity thresholds used in the classifier based on observed response quality. We evaluate CALLS on four classes of enterprise tasks: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), code assistance, long-document summarization, and question answering, and demonstrate that it decreases inference cost on a corpus of 48k production queries by 61.4% while losing only 3.2% of its quality relative to serving all traffic through a large model. Compared with state-of-the-art adaptive nearest cohort techniques, CALLS yields an additional 14.7% improvement with negligible quality loss.
candidates.reason: CALLSはクエリ複雑度の軽量分類器と3階層ルーティング方策、オンライン較正により大規模企業システムでのLLM呼び出しをコスト・品質のトレードオフで振り分ける戦略であり、推論基盤のルーティング／負荷分散への直接の貢献である。

candidates.title: FineGates: LLMs Finetuning with Compression using Stochastic Gates
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), with billions of parameters, present significant challenges for full finetuning due to the high computational demands, memory requirements, and impracticality of many real-world applications. When faced with limited computational resources or small datasets, updating all model parameters can often result in overfitting. To address this, lightweight finetuning techniques have been proposed, like learning low-rank adapter layers. These methods aim to train only a few additional parameters combined with the base model, which remains frozen, reducing resource usage and mitigating overfitting risks. In this work, we propose an adaptor model based on stochastic gates that simultaneously sparsify the frozen base model with task-specific adaptation. Our method comes with a small number of trainable parameters and allows us to speed up the base model inference with competitive accuracy. We evaluate it in additional variants by equipping it with additional low-rank parameters and comparing it to several recent baselines. Our results show that the proposed method improves the finetuned model accuracy comparatively to the several baselines and allows the removal of up to 20-40\% without significant accuracy loss.
candidates.reason: FineGatesは確率的ゲートで凍結した基底モデル自体をタスク適応と同時にスパース化し、パラメータの20〜40%除去と基底モデルの推論高速化を実現する手法であり、微調整を内部手段として推論側の圧縮・高速化に直接つながる。
